title: U.S. Chamber: 2026 Empowering Small Business
claim: Reports 66% AI use and widespread upskilling among AI users.
caveat: Self-reported adoption and correlations, not causal income evidence; advocacy organization.

title: NFIB Small Business Technology Survey
claim: Reports 24% AI use; resource constraints and business-size differences.
caveat: Different date, population and instrument from S01; never combine into one adoption estimate.

title: Upwork In-Demand Skills 2026
claim: AI integration, video editing and chatbot development appear among growing skills; based on completed-job earnings.
caveat: Platform-specific, vendor interest; growth is not a beginner success rate or individual income forecast.

title: JPMorgan Chase Institute: Understanding AI use by small businesses
claim: Measures payments to identified AI services rather than only stated adoption; usage differs by industry and firm size.
caveat: Misses free tools and some bundled or unrecognized payments; spending on tools does not establish spending on consultants.

title: NAR 2025 Technology Survey release
claim: 46% report AI-generated content; 46% report no noticeable business impact from AI.
caveat: Member sample; tool use is not proof agents will buy our proposed package.

title: Thomson Reuters Future of Professionals 2026
geography: Global; 1,816 legal, tax, audit and related professionals
claim: Describes a gap between AI strategies, staff training and everyday implementation.
caveat: Not a US-only or small-firm sample; vendor sells professional AI.

title: National Restaurant Association: Future of Restaurant Technology
geography: US; 212 operators and eight leader interviews
claim: Reports integration, cost, skills and business-fit barriers; 38.6% use AI tools.
caveat: Sponsored by DoorDash and PayPal; bounded operator sample.

title: AMA Physician Survey on Augmented Intelligence
type: Primary association survey landing page; opened
claim: Confirms ongoing physician AI adoption research.
caveat: Landing page alone does not substantiate detailed estimates; use S09 for administrative-use discussion.

title: AMA: Physicians' greatest use for AI—administrative burdens
claim: Administrative work is a reported opportunity area.
caveat: Historical, excerpt-only; does not validate any specific clinical product or price.

title: AGC 2026 Construction Hiring and Business Outlook
claim: Discusses productivity, technology investment and operational pressures.
caveat: Use-or-plan-to-invest is not actual deployment; contractors vary substantially in size.

title: Shopify Magic product descriptions
geography: Global product available to US merchants
claim: Basic AI product-description generation is included in Shopify plans.
caveat: Important competing substitute; feature availability is not merchant willingness to pay.

title: Gumroad pricing
claim: Lists direct-sale fee of 10% + $0.50 and Discover fee of 30%.
caveat: Platform fees only; income tax, refunds, labor and acquisition costs remain separate.

title: Intercom pricing
claim: Fin starts at $0.99 per outcome with plan/channel qualifications.
caveat: Product cost comparator, not agency rates; seat and usage charges can apply.

title: Zapier pricing explanation
date: 2026 page; exact publication day not captured
claim: Professional advertised at $19.99/month billed annually, with task limits.
caveat: Indicative only; recheck actual checkout and AI usage charges before quoting.

title: OpenAI: Plugins in ChatGPT
claim: Plugins package instructions, connected apps and skills; availability and sharing depend on permissions.
caveat: Do not confuse current plugins with the earlier plugin product; directory listing is not proof of monetization.

title: OpenAI: Custom GPT retirement and migration FAQ
claim: Describes migration to plugins; custom actions require separate replacement and testing.
caveat: Recheck customer account notices; do not promise universal dates, access or automatic migration.

title: Reddit: Making money doing AI automation
date: Relative date only: approximately 3 months before retrieval
claim: Comments emphasize narrow niches, demonstrable time savings, maintenance and fragile workflows.
caveat: Anonymous self-reports, promotion and selection bias; revenue assertions not verified.

title: Reddit: Struggling to find a first client
date: Relative date only: approximately 5 months before retrieval
claim: Original poster reports outreach without customers; discussion distinguishes selling from technical building.
caveat: One self-report; cannot derive conversion rates or market prevalence.

title: Ethan Mollick: Multiplayer AI discussion on LinkedIn
date: Relative date shown: 1 month before retrieval; edited
claim: Raises organizational coordination and shared-context challenges.
caveat: Expert interpretation, not a purchasing survey; displayed dates can differ from index dates.

title: Wharton faculty profile: Ethan Mollick
claim: Verifies research and teaching role in management and generative AI.
caveat: Credential establishes relevant expertise, not correctness of every prediction.

title: Simon Willison: About and disclosures
type: First-party identity and business disclosure; opened
claim: Documents open-source products, consulting/training and paid research briefings.
caveat: Self-description; no audited earnings; sponsors and other commercial relationships disclosed.

title: Pieter Levels interview transcript, Lex Fridman #440
claim: Describes rapid product experiments, payment validation and multiple failed launches.
caveat: Survivorship bias; claims are the founder's account, not independently audited revenue.

title: Ethan Mollick X post on research productivity
date: 2025 indexed post; exact date not independently confirmed
type: Search excerpt only; direct fetch returned 403
claim: Indexed post discusses a research finding about AI and academic productivity.
caveat: Not used for numerical conclusions; underlying study and full thread not verified.

title: Pieter Levels X profile
claim: Records an access limitation; use S22 for readable original material.
caveat: Not evidence for demand or earnings. X automated trending summaries were excluded.

title: LinkedIn Work Change: How Small Businesses Can Win in 2026
geography: Global with separately identified US measures
claim: Discusses AI literacy, trusted brands and professional networks in small business.
caveat: Profiles, platform signals and surveys are different measures; not a revenue dataset.

title: TechSoup: Love INC Copilot implementation case
claim: Describes administrative, communication and reporting uses supported by implementation coaching.
caveat: Microsoft-supported case; no controlled ROI or independent consultant fee disclosure.

title: NAIC: Artificial Intelligence
claim: Lists insurance applications and emphasizes human oversight, fairness and insurer responsibility.
caveat: Industry context; does not establish independent agents' budgets or replace state-specific review.

title: SHRM 2025 AI policy talking points
geography: HR research; geography not confirmed from excerpt
claim: Mentions recruiting, learning and HR system uses.
caveat: Excerpt-only; broad direction, no adoption percentages used in our conclusions.

title: USDA ERS: Precision agriculture by farm size
claim: Technology adoption differs sharply by farm size.
caveat: Precision agriculture is broader than generative AI; weak context for our farm-administration hypotheses.

title: HubSpot: 2026 State of Marketing
claim: Discusses AI content, media creation and administrative workflows.
caveat: Global and vendor-sponsored; not evidence of US freelancer earnings.

title: Simon Willison: Agentic engineering guides
claim: Guides cover testing, review and agentic coding practices.
caveat: Technical education, not market-size or income evidence.

title: TechSoup: Should your nonprofit use AI in grantseeking?
claim: Identifies grantseeking as an AI discussion area.
caveat: Need full guidance and funder-specific rules before delivery; does not establish win rates.
